guideTitle: 6 Best Extra Long Non Slip Bath Mats in 2026
metaTitle: Best Extra Long Non Slip Bath Mats in 2026
metaDescription: Six extra long tub mats from 39 to 40 inches compared by suction cup count, drain holes, material and how well each covers a long tub floor.
mainKeyword: extra long non slip bath mat
introParagraphs: A standard bath mat is about 28 to 35 inches long, which leaves bare tub floor at one end of a long tub, exactly where a foot might land when you step in or turn. An extra long mat of 39 or 40 inches closes that gap. The tradeoff is that a longer mat has more edge to curl, more surface to dry and a bigger need to match the shape of your tub floor, so the details matter more than the length alone.

The six mats here are the Linoows 40 by 16 inch with 300 suction cups, the OTHWAY 39 by 17 inch TPE mat with a detachable hair catcher, the CADONO 40 by 16 inch with 200 cups, the HITSLAM 40 by 16 inch loofah-style mat with no suction cups, the Naoloture 40 by 16 inch with 200 cups and 176 drain holes and the ENKOSI 40 by 16 inch with 200 cups and an honest note about surfaces.

We evaluated each on length, width, grip mechanism, drainage and material, and on what the listing says about the floor it needs. Measure the flat floor of your tub before ordering, because a long mat that runs up the curved ends will not lie flat and can lift at the edges. Length is the headline, but fit and floor decide whether it works.

products.name: Linoows Bathtub Mat, 40x16 Inch, 300 Suction Cups
products.description:
Linoows leads this lineup on the number it states: 300 high-strength, flexible suction cups on a 40 by 16 inch mat, which the listing says is 30 percent more cups than other mats. The top has 300 bubbles designed like pebbles for a gentle massage feel and a lychee-textured surface for reliable grip, and the listing says the mat is 30 percent longer than standard and has an excellent drainage system. For a long tub, the cup count spreads the hold across the whole length.

Cup count matters more as a mat gets longer, because a long mat has more room for one end to lift. A fine, lychee-style texture gives feet a grippy but not harsh surface. As with every suction mat here, the cups need a smooth, non-porous floor, and the listing gives no drain hole count in the text we have.

Compared with the CADONO and Naoloture it lists more cups, and compared with the OTHWAY it has a lower stated width. It suits a long, smooth tub where holding both ends of the mat is the concern. If you set it down starting from the drain end and press toward the far end, trapped air escapes more evenly and more cups engage.
products.bestFor: Holding both ends of a long mat on a smooth tub.
pros: 40 in length covers a long tub
cons: Drain hole count is not stated in the text we have
40 in may run up curved tub ends

products.name: OTHWAY Long Bathtub Mat, 39 x 17 Inch, Hair Catcher
products.description:
OTHWAY adds a feature no other mat here has: a detachable hair catcher that blocks hair from going down the drain. The mat is 39 by 17 inches, wider than the 16-inch standard, in recyclable TPE the listing calls thick, durable and odorless, with big drain holes. It claims 35 percent more coverage than regular mats.

A hair catcher saves a plumbing headache, and a wider mat gives more room for your feet. TPE is soft and low-odor, and thick TPE has some weight, which helps it stay put. The listing does not state a cup count in the text we have, so confirm the grip details before buying.

Compared with the 40-inch mats it is an inch shorter but an inch wider, and compared with the HITSLAM it uses cups. It suits a long tub where hair clogging the drain is a recurring problem. Because the listing is thin on grip details, read the full page for how the underside is built before ordering.
products.bestFor: Tubs where hair clogs the drain.
pros: 39 by 17 in is wider than most
cons: Cup count is not stated in the text we have

products.name: CADONO Extra Long Bathtub Mat, 40x16 Clear, 200 Cups
products.description:
CADONO's clear 40 by 16 inch mat is made of flexible BPA-free material with a pebble-textured, domed topside, a fine non-slip texture on the surface and 200 powerful suction cups underneath. The listing says hundreds of drain holes remove water quickly and help prevent stagnation. The domed top is soft underfoot.

Two hundred cups is a solid number for a 40-inch mat, and the fine texture adds grip without roughness. A clear mat shows less color on the tub, which some people prefer and others find hard to see. The listing does not state a hole count in the text we have.

Compared with the Linoows it has fewer cups, and compared with the Naoloture it is clear rather than black. It suits a buyer who wants a long, soft, clear mat at a moderate cup count. A clear mat is also the one that hides least when the tub is stained, so keep the floor clean. A mat this wide also leaves less bare floor at the sides, which is welcome for anyone who shuffles when stepping in.
products.bestFor: A long clear mat with a soft domed top.
cons: Clear mat is harder to see on a white tub
Hole count is not stated in the text we have

products.name: Naoloture Extra Long Bathtub Mat, Black, 40x16, 176 Drain Holes
products.description:
Naoloture states both counts: 200 large suction cups and 176 drain holes on a black 40 by 16 inch mat, with a claim of 30 percent more coverage than regular mats. The listing says the large cups are more grippy and that the holes let water flow easily under the mat and down the drain. A black mat is easy to see against a white tub.

Visibility is a quiet safety benefit, since a dark mat on a light floor is easy to spot and check for shifting. Stated numbers let you compare directly: it has fewer cups than the Linoows and a stated hole count that the others lack. The black finish may show soap film and hard-water spots.

Compared with the ENKOSI it is nearly identical in size and cup count and adds a drain figure, and compared with the CADONO it is black and states holes. It suits a buyer who wants a visible mat and stated drainage. Rinse the black surface after each shower, because hard-water film is easier to see on dark mats than on clear ones. The mat's flexible body lets it curve slightly with the floor, which helps at the ends.
products.bestFor: A highly visible mat with stated drainage.
pros: Black mat is easy to see on a light tub
cons: Black shows soap film and spots

products.name: ENKOSI Non-Slip Bath Mat, 40x16 Extra Long, Black
products.description:
ENKOSI is the listing that says the quiet part out loud: its 200 suction cups anchor to smooth, non-porous tub and shower floors and will not hold on textured, refinished or similar surfaces. The mat is 40 by 16 inches and described as covering far more of the tub floor than a standard mat, fitting standard and extra-long tubs. The honesty about surfaces is a useful guide.

A mat that tells you where it will not work saves a return and a slip. If your floor is smooth and glazed, 200 cups on a 40-inch mat is a strong setup. The listing does not give a drain hole count or material in the text we have.

Compared with the Naoloture it is similar in size and cups with clearer surface limits, and compared with the HITSLAM it relies on suction. It suits a smooth tub and a buyer who values straightforward limits. If you ever move to a home with a different tub, the same mat would need the same smooth floor to work.
products.bestFor: A smooth tub and a listing that is honest about limits.
pros: Clear note on which surfaces it will not hold on
40 by 16 in covers a long tub
cons: Drain holes and material are not stated in the text we have
Will not hold on textured or refinished floors

products.name: HITSLAM Non Slip Bathtub Mat, 40 x 16 Inch, Suction-Free Loofah
products.description:
HITSLAM offers the long mat without suction: a 40 by 16 inch soft PVC loofah-style mat with a durable plaid backing that the listing says holds it firmly in place even on wet surfaces. The hollow loop surface combined with a lattice bottom creates many drain holes for fast drainage. It is the pick for floors where cups will not seal.

A suction-free design is useful on textured or refinished tubs, but it relies on friction, so it may slide more on a smooth floor than a cup mat. The loop surface is soft and rinses easily. The listing does not state a weight figure in the text we have.

Compared with the cup-based mats it avoids pulling at a finish and is easier to lift, and compared with the OTHWAY it uses a plaid backing instead of cups. It suits a long tub whose floor will not accept suction. Wring or shake it after showers and hang it over the tub edge so that both sides dry.
products.bestFor: A long tub whose floor will not seal suction cups.
pros: No suction cups, avoids pulling at a finish
Plaid backing grips wet surfaces, per the listing
Hollow loop and lattice drain quickly
cons: Relies on friction and may slide on a smooth floor
Weight is not stated in the text we have

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 40-inch mat needs 40 inches of flat floor, and many tubs curve up at the ends or narrow toward the drain. A mat that rides up the curve lifts at the edges and invites a slip. Measure from end to end along the flat bottom, and subtract a couple of inches. If your tub is shorter, a trim-to-fit mat or a standard size is better.

The Linoows lists 300 cups, the CADONO, Naoloture and ENKOSI list 200 and the OTHWAY gives no count in the text we have. A long mat has more room for one end to lift, so a high cup count helps. Cups still need a smooth floor. Check that both ends seal when you press them down.

The OTHWAY is 17 inches wide, and the others are 16 inches. An inch of width adds a little standing room. Most tubs have 16 inches or more of flat width, but narrow ones do not. Measure the width at the narrowest point.

The Naoloture states 176 drain holes, the CADONO lists hundreds and the HITSLAM uses a hollow loop and lattice. The OTHWAY adds a detachable hair catcher. Good drainage reduces mildew and lifting, and a hair catcher protects the drain. Lift the mat after each shower regardless.

Black mats like the Naoloture and ENKOSI contrast with a white tub and are easy to see. Clear mats like the CADONO blend in. If vision is not sharp, choose a contrasting color. A visible mat also shows when it has shifted.

The ENKOSI states that its cups will not hold on textured or refinished floors, and the same is true of every cup mat here. If your floor is textured, the HITSLAM suction-free design is the fit. Press a hand on the floor to judge. If the floor is smooth glazed porcelain or acrylic, cups are usually the right answer, and a textured or refinished floor calls for a different type of mat.

howWeEvaluated.title: Length and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared lengths of 39 and 40 inches and widths of 16 and 17 inches, and noted the need to measure the flat floor. Fit counted more than the headline length. We judged how each long mat would behave at its ends, since that is where a 40-inch mat is most likely to lift.

howWeEvaluated.title: Grip mechanism
howWeEvaluated.description: Cup counts from 200 to 300 and the HITSLAM plaid backing were compared. We read surface limits, such as the ENKOSI note. Honest limits earned credit. Stated cup and drain counts were credited, and the surface limits that listings admit were treated as a mark of honesty.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drainage and hygiene
howWeEvaluated.description: Drain holes, the Naoloture 176 count, the hollow loop of the HITSLAM and the OTHWAY hair catcher were compared. Quick drainage and drain protection scored well. We assumed buyers will measure their tub, and flagged the listings where the width or length might not fit common tubs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Visibility and comfort
howWeEvaluated.description: Color, texture and softness were compared. Black mats stand out, clear mats blend, and domed or loofah tops differ underfoot. We weighed visibility as a safety factor. The hair catcher on the OTHWAY was treated as a thoughtful feature that solves a real household problem.

howWeEvaluated.title: Maintenance
howWeEvaluated.description: Material and washing needs were compared, including TPE, PVC and BPA-free claims. We favored mats that are easy to lift, rinse and dry. We considered the weight and bulk of a longer mat when it has to be lifted, rinsed and dried every day.

howToChoose.note: Fit and floor matter more than the length on the label.

faq.q: Is a longer bath mat better?
faq.a: It gives more coverage, which helps in a long tub, but only if your tub floor is flat for that length. A 40-inch mat on a short or curved tub will ride up. Measure first. A wide margin of a few inches at each end of the tub helps, since a mat that touches the end wall tends to curl.

faq.q: How many suction cups do I need?
faq.a: More cups spread the hold across a longer mat. The Linoows lists 300 and several others 200. Cup count matters less than a clean, smooth floor and a firm press. Some people press the mat with the palm of the hand in a spiral from the center outward to seat the cups evenly.

faq.q: Why might the ends of my long mat lift?
faq.a: Curved tub ends, soap film or a textured floor can keep cups from sealing. Clean the floor, press the ends and check the fit. If it keeps lifting, the mat may be too long. If you share the bathroom, a mat of a visible color helps a second person see whether it has shifted.

faq.q: What does a hair catcher do?
faq.a: The OTHWAY hair catcher blocks hair from going down the drain, saving you from clogs. It needs emptying regularly. It is helpful in a household with long hair. For a very long tub, check that the mat does not run over the drain, which can block water.

faq.q: Can I use these on a textured tub?
faq.a: Not the cup mats, because suction needs a smooth floor, as the ENKOSI listing says. The HITSLAM is suction-free. Test any mat with a firm foot shove. A weekly cold wash or a scrub with mild soap removes the film that makes cups lose grip.

faq.q: How should I clean a long mat?
faq.a: Lift it after each shower, rinse both sides and hang to dry. Wash weekly with mild soap, or machine wash if the listing allows. A clean mat and floor grip better. Replace a mat when its cups no longer grip or its surface wears smooth, even if it still looks fine.
